result.description:
Head Chef – Surly's Surry Hills

Position Title: Head Chef
Reports To: General Manager
Business: Surly's Hospitality Pty Ltd
Venue: Surly's American Tavern
Location: 182 Campbell Street, Surry Hills NSW 2010
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Salary: AUD $85,000 per annum plus statutory superannuation

Position Summary

The Head Chef is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the kitchen operations at Surly's American Tavern. This is a full-time senior management position responsible for menu development, food quality, kitchen leadership, financial performance, compliance with food safety legislation, and the efficient operation of a high-volume commercial kitchen.

The role is integral to the ongoing success of the business and requires an experienced chef capable of leading a diverse kitchen team while maintaining consistently high culinary standards, operational efficiency, and profitability.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

- Manage and oversee the daily operations of the kitchen, ensuring efficient service and consistently high food quality.
- Develop, design and implement seasonal menus, daily specials, catering packages and function menus that align with the Surly's brand.
- Plan recipes, portion sizes and menu pricing to maximise profitability while maintaining quality and consistency.
Supervise all food preparation and cooking to ensure presentation, quality, portion control and customer satisfaction standards are consistently achieved.
- Recruit, train, mentor and supervise kitchen employees including Sous Chefs, Chef de Parties, Commis Chefs, Apprentices and Kitchen Hands.
- Prepare staff rosters and allocate duties to ensure efficient kitchen operations and appropriate labour utilisation.
- Monitor labour costs, food costs, gross profit margins and kitchen productivity to achieve business budgets and financial targets.
- Order food, beverages and kitchen supplies, manage supplier relationships and negotiate purchasing where appropriate.
- Monitor inventory levels and implement stock control systems to minimise wastage and maximise profitability.
- Ensure compliance with all Food Safety Standards, HACCP principles, NSW Food Authority requirements and Work Health and Safety legislation.
- Develop, implement and continuously improve kitchen procedures, systems and operational standards.
- Coordinate preventative maintenance of kitchen equipment and arrange repairs as required.
- Work collaboratively with senior management on marketing initiatives, promotional campaigns, special events and business development opportunities.
- Monitor customer feedback and implement continuous improvements to menu offerings and kitchen performance.
- Maintain accurate records relating to stock control, food cost analysis, labour costs, wastage and kitchen performance.
- Ensure high standards of cleanliness, hygiene and food handling practices are maintained throughout the kitchen at all times.
- Foster a positive, professional and high-performing kitchen culture focused on teamwork, accountability and continuous improvement.
- Drive culinary innovation while maintaining the authentic American barbecue style and quality standards that define the Surly's brand.

Skills, Qualifications and Experience

The successful candidate will possess:

- Certificate IV in Commercial Cookery (or equivalent recognised qualification).
- A minimum of five (5) years' relevant experience in a senior chef or Head Chef position.
- Demonstrated experience managing a high-volume commercial kitchen.
- Proven leadership and people management skills with the ability to recruit, train and develop kitchen staff.
- Strong understanding of menu planning, recipe development, food costing and inventory management.
- Excellent knowledge of budgeting, labour management and cost control.
- Comprehensive understanding of Australian food safety legislation, HACCP principles and workplace health and safety requirements.
- Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure while maintaining high standards of food quality and customer service.
- Strong commitment to continuous improvement, innovation and operational excellence.

Key Performance Outcomes

The Head Chef will be expected to:

- Deliver consistently high-quality food and presentation standards.
- Maintain food and labour costs within approved budgets.
- Lead, develop and retain a high-performing kitchen team.
- Ensure full compliance with food safety and workplace health and safety requirements.
- Support the commercial success of the business through effective menu engineering, operational efficiency and cost management.
- Contribute to the ongoing growth and reputation of Surly's American Tavern through culinary leadership and innovation.

JBS Australia is the largest and most respected meat and food producer in Australia. We have a strong portfolio of leading and renowned beef, lamb, pork, salmon and value-added branded products, such as AMH, Swift, Primo, Murray Valley and Huon. JBS Australia is a part of the global JBS business, the largest animal protein business in the world, and the second largest food company, with operations in North America, South America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

The JBS Dinmore Processing Plant is the largest beef facility in the southern hemisphere. Located near Ipswich, in south east Queensland, the facility has a daily production ability of 3,400 cattle and employs approximately 2,600 people. Cattle are sourced from the finest cattle producing regions to produce a diverse range of pasture fed and grain beef products, from commodity to premium. The renowned AMH brand, the award-winning Yardstick, the highly marbled grain fed Pure Prime and our state’s brand, Queenslander Beef and more are all produced at Dinmore.

About the Role:
We are currently seeking a Mechanical Engineering Technician to join our Dinmore Plant. We are seeking a passionate and energetic individual who is committed to the position and providing an effective professional service. This is a fantastic opportunity to join our dynamic, exciting organization who are the leaders in safety and culture across Australia. Within the role you will enjoy the benefits and satisfaction in contributing to the continued growth and success of our business. This role will be responsible for providing maintenance support to all areas across the plant to ensure the attainment of Production, Quality/FSQA, and Workplace Health and Safety requirements and objectives. This is a full-time position with the annual salary more than $79,423 plus superannuation.

Your key responsibilities will include:
Conducts tests of mechanical systems, collects and analyses data, and assembles and installs mechanical assemblies in support of Mechanical Engineers and Engineering Technologists.
Ensuring maximum equipment uptime is achieved by providing effective and efficient mechanical preventative and breakdown maintenance
Engaging in fabrication, installation and repair of mechanical machines, instruments or appliances
Ensuring that all work is carried out to the Company and requirements and conforms to all relevant regulations
Utilising fault-finding to troubleshoot and rectify problems

About you
Previous experience in a fast-paced industrial manufacturing environment
Previous experience within the meat industry advantageous
Sound knowledge of pneumatics and hydraulics, as well as a basic knowledge of electrics and welding skills
Excellent interpersonal skills
Demonstrated continuous improvement approach
Ability to support a broad variety of mechanical work
High level of accuracy and attention to detail
Ability to communicate at all levels
Ability to work autonomously as well as in a team environment
Ability to work various shifts
Full Australian working rights

Why work for us:
Retail discounts with national partners
Health insurance discounts on Bupa Health and Medibank
Heavily discounted meat products

The ad is valid for 28 days.

What next? If you’re passionate and want to be a part of the largest meat, pork and salmon manufacturer and producer in Australia, this opportunity may be for you. Apply now!

About our Organisation

AVK is a highly respected global business and one of the leading valve manufacturers in the water supply, wastewater, civil infrastructure, gas, fire protection and industrial sectors. The AVK Group operates more than 100 companies worldwide, supplying to more than 80 countries and employs around 5,300 people. AVK's core business is the design and manufacture of valves, hydrants, fitting, clamps, and accessories each complying with the highest standards of quality, safety, and durability. In addition to the products, AVK Smart Water systems provide digital solutions for AVK core products through intelligent IoT-based platform as a new way for asset owners to monitor water infrastructure. 
AVK Australia is part of the Global AVK Group and responsible for the group’s activities in the Oceania region (Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea & Pacific Islands). AVK Australia is based in Wingfield, South Australia, with operations across Australia as well as New Zealand.

About the Role 

We are currently seeking a Governance & Commercial Legal Advisor to join our team on a permanent full-time basis. 

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Governance & Commercial Legal Advisor will be responsible for supporting organisational governance, regulatory compliance, internal controls and business risk management across the organisation.

The position provides advice and support to management and project delivery teams through risk management initiatives, analysis of organisational information and data, and implementation of processes that ensure compliance with regulatory and governance requirements.

Key Responsibilities

•	Working with Project Delivery team develop and implement systems for document control, including approvals and version controls
•	Analysis of project costs and forecasts to identify potential for variations and forecast project profitability
•	Analysing project performance data to support organisational planning, decision-making and process optimisation
•	Reviewing contracts and templates to ensure regulatory compliance and analyse to identify potential risks
•	Develop, review and maintain organisational policies, procedures, templates and governance documentation
•	Analyse and assess government and industry programs, including grant programs, and identify opportunities for the company to participate
•	Develop a "Tender Toolbox" for use in Project Tender Submissions, containing relevant Governance and Compliance documentation
•	Administration of Regulatory Compliance Program
•	Support the implementation of risk management IT systems in HSE, Quality and HR operations
•	Assist business managers to design, develop and implement corrective action programs to address legal compliance risks and / or adapt to changes in the regulatory environment
•	Analyse duty costs, identify opportunities for duty drawback claims, and administer regular claims
•	Maintain governance registers and organisational records relating to corporate assets and compliance obligations

Skills & Experience

•	A relevant Bachelor Degree or higher and a minimum of 12 months relevant experience. 5 years’ experience may be considered in lieu of qualification
•	Experience reviewing contracts, policies and governance documents 
•	Ability to analyse data and other information to support forecasting and decision-making
•	Ability to engage with stakeholders to coordinate effective organisational outcomes
•	Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities
•	Strong verbal and written communication skills

If this sounds like the job for you, then please apply now by submitting your CV and a covering letter, in Word format, addressing the selection criteria.  

Visit our website http://www.avkcivil.com.au to learn more about the company, or our global website www.avkvalves.com to learn more about the AVK Group in general.

At Black & More, we look for people who want to own their work, deliver great projects, and grow into professionals who make a difference to society.  We're a values-led company and give our people the opportunity and responsibility to lead real outcomes for communities. If you want to be trusted with meaningful work and to challenge yourself, you'll find purpose with us. Step Beyond the Workshop with BDGT - Technical Sales Engineer

Are you a trade qualified machinist or engineer ready to take your career in a new direction? If you enjoy solving technical problems and working with customers but still want to stay connected to the machining industry, this could be the opportunity you've been looking for.

For more than 50 years, BDGT has earned a reputation for precision, innovation, and engineering excellence. We partner with clients across the resources, packaging, construction, and manufacturing sectors to design and manufacture specialised components, machinery, and equipment.

Offering complete in house capability across machining, fabrication, assembly, refurbishment, and finishing, BDGT delivers end to end solutions and prides itself on quality workmanship and exceptional customer service.
The Opportunity:

As our Technical Sales Engineer, you'll draw on your engineering and machining background to provide practical solutions for customers and guide projects from concept through to completion. You will work closely with clients, suppliers, and our production teams, you'll become the link between customer requirements and successful project delivery.
Key Responsibilities:

    Develop and maintain strong relationships with customers and key stakeholders
    Respond to technical enquiries and recommend fit for purpose solutions
    Review engineering drawings and specifications to prepare quotations and proposals
    Coordinate material requirements and supplier engagement
    Liaise with production teams to ensure projects remain on track
    Oversee project timelines and delivery milestones
    Provide technical guidance and support throughout the project lifecycle

What We're Looking For:

    Trade qualification in Engineering (Cert III) or a Mechanical Engineering qualification
    Experience working within machining, CNC, or manufacturing environments
    Sound understanding of manufacturing processes and engineering drawings
    Strong communication skills with the ability to build lasting relationships
    A solutions focused approach and strong problem solving capability
    Good commercial acumen and the ability to juggle multiple priorities

Why Join BDGT?

Take the Next Step: Transition your engineering career into a technical and commercial role.

Interesting Projects: Work with customers across a range of industries on complex and rewarding projects.

Great Team Environment: Join an experienced and supportive team that values collaboration and initiative.

Established Business: Become part of a respected company with a long history of success and continued growth.

If you're looking to use your machining expertise in a role that offers variety, responsibility, and long term career development, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and be a part of something exceptional!

For a confidential discussion, contact Lucy Boyle on 03 9116 7465.

Better and fairer care. Always.

We are St Vincent's Health Australia, Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services.

Founded by The Sisters of Charity in 1857, our +30,000 healthcare superheroes operate public and private hospitals, residential aged care, community and virtual care, and outreach programs.

About the role

Be part of a busy and collaborative team providing first and second-level technical support for computer systems, software, and hardware issues, both remotely and face-to-face. Troubleshoot, monitor, and restore personal computers and devices connected to the network

Deliver high-quality client service, managing issues with integrity, compassion, and timely resolution

Work from various sites across our Hospital and Aged Care network in NSW to resolve technical incidents

Current Australian driver's license and reliable vehicle is a MUST Certificate IV in Information Technology Support (or equivalent experience)

Lead Safety. Build Culture. Make a Real Difference.

Are you a passionate safety professional who knows that great safety outcomes are built on trust, influence and genuine engagement with people?

We are seeking an experienced Safety Manager to join a diverse and growing organisation based in Wangaratta, supporting a workforce of approximately 300 employees across multiple operational environments including manufacturing, warehousing and field-based technical services.

This is an opportunity to step into a highly visible leadership role where you will shape safety strategy, influence business performance and help create a workplace where everyone goes home safe every day.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will lead and drive the Health, Safety and Wellbeing function across multiple sites and operational activities. You will develop, implement and continuously improve safety systems, ensuring compliance while fostering a practical, positive and people-focused safety culture.

You will be responsible for:

* Developing, implementing and managing the organisation's OHS Operational Plan
* Acting as the organisation's Return to Work (RTW) Coordinator
* Leading risk management activities, including hazard identification, risk assessments and controls
* Delivering and coordinating safety training, coaching and capability development
* Supporting managers and employees with task design, reasonable adjustments and injury prevention initiatives
* Facilitating meaningful consultation with employees, Health and Safety Representatives and key stakeholders
* Leading incident investigations using recognised methodologies such as ICAM, Root Cause Analysis and other contemporary investigation techniques
* Ensuring corrective actions are practical, effective and embedded into business operations
* Maintaining compliance with legislative, regulatory and reporting requirements
* Managing safety records, reporting systems and digital safety management tools
* Developing safety metrics, reporting insights and recommendations to support business decision-making
* Driving continuous improvement across all safety and wellbeing programs

About You

You are more than a compliance professional, you are a genuine leader who can connect with people, earn trust and positively influence behaviours at every level of an organisation.

You will bring:

Essential Requirements

* Minimum Certificate IV in Work Health & Safety or Occupational Health & Safety
* Demonstrated experience in a similar Safety Manager, Safety Advisor or Health & Safety leadership role within manufacturing, industrial, logistics, warehousing, technical services or a comparable operational environment
* Experience as a Return to Work Coordinator
* Strong capability in risk management, safety systems and operational safety leadership
* Proven experience leading complex incident investigations and implementing sustainable corrective actions
* Excellent knowledge of reporting procedures, record-keeping requirements and safety management systems
* Strong understanding and application of digital reporting and safety management platforms

Comprehensive knowledge of:
* Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Victoria)
* Victorian OHS Regulations
* Relevant Australian Standards and industry best practice
* Current driver's licence

Personal Attributes
We are looking for someone who:

* Leads with authenticity, integrity and accountability
* Has an open, approachable and engaging communication style
* Can confidently influence and coach leaders, supervisors and frontline employees
* Builds strong relationships across all levels of the organisation and with external stakeholders
* Balances commercial understanding with a genuine commitment to safety and legal compliance
* Is highly organised, proactive and solutions-focused
* Thrives in a hands-on environment and enjoys being visible in the workplace rather than behind a desk

Why Join Us?

* Attractive $100K++ salary and benefits package
* Key leadership position with genuine influence across the organisation
* Diverse operational environment providing variety and challenge
* Opportunity to shape safety culture and drive meaningful change
* Work with a business that values people, safety and continuous improvement
* Enjoy the lifestyle benefits of living and working in beautiful regional Wangaratta

Ready to Lead the Way?

If you're a people-first safety professional with the experience, credibility and passion to create safer workplaces and stronger safety cultures, we'd love to hear from you.

Contact Dan Sawyer for a PD and more information in confidence on 0403 899143
